headline: High-risk Devin↔mem0 pairing: Devin’s broad write/network/OAuth powers can drive cascading actions and data leakage into mem0-backed memory flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers; mem0 is a knowledge-management layer that may ingest agent outputs. The pair has a plausible content-to-instruction bridge, but no documented shared channel or direct parser details. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Devin writes attacker-controlled text into a shared memory store or MCP-backed note that mem0 later reuses as instructions
IF mem0 is configured to feed retrieved memories back into Devin without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable automatic reuse of mem0 memories as instructions
Add provenance tags to all shared notes
Restrict MCP tools to allowlisted schemas
Manually review any memory item before reuse

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles secrets via GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion scopes; mem0 is a memory system that can persist and surface content. Even without explicit shared storage, the pair can move sensitive work data into longer-lived memory, creating leakage risk beyond default expectations.
conditions: IF Devin stores repo secrets, chat excerpts, or issue text into mem0 memory
IF mem0 persists or replays those items across sessions or tenants
mitigations: Block secrets from being written to memory
Redact chat and ticket content before ingestion
Set short retention on shared memories
Audit memory writes for sensitive fields

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted cloud-workspace shell, filesystem write, git modification, and broad network egress; mem0 is open-source but its runtime write surfaces are not documented here. Because Devin clearly has strong mutation powers and the pair may target shared mutable resources, uncertainty escalates to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF mem0 is deployed with write access to the same repository, database, or memory store Devin edits
IF both agents operate on the same mutable resource without locking or optimistic concurrency
mitigations: Separate write targets per agent
Enable locking on shared resources
Assign one agent read-only access
Require manual merge for git or memory writes
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act in a planner-executor loop and write to GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion; mem0 can preserve and replay prior outputs. If Devin’s outputs are treated as authoritative by mem0-backed retrieval or downstream workflows, errors can cascade into real actions or commits.
conditions: IF mem0 returns Devin-generated content as authoritative context
IF downstream automation uses that context to file tickets, send messages, or commit code
mitigations: Require verification before acting on retrieved memories
Add human approval for outbound writes
Limit mem0 to advisory-only retrieval
Log and diff all action-triggering memories
requires-engineering: insert validation gates before external side effects

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is documented to handle source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and integration tokens, while mem0 is a memory store with no residency or retention controls shown here. The mismatch is mainly about retention and subject-rights handling on shared work data, not a proven regulated-data breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data from chat, tickets, or docs is written into mem0
IF mem0 retention or deletion behavior differs from the source system's policy
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from memory
Mirror deletion requests into mem0
Document retention for shared memories
Review residency settings before deployment
